title: Slot-slicing warmup variance notes
content:
Context / quick goal:
- Trying to understand why cold-to-warm latency variance is high for multi-tenant pools when we attempt to pre-warm by 'slot slicing' (small warmup-only batches assigned to different logical slots on the GPU).
- Experiment objective: 3 controls (no-slicing baseline, fixed-slice, adaptive-slice) across two arrival patterns (zipf-ish spikes, steady ramp). Measure p50/p95/p99 tail behavior during first 60s after capacity scale-up and under mixed KV-cache hit rates.

Hypothesis:
- Slot-slicing reduces steady-state contention during warmup but increases variance in early p99 because slices race for kernel init + KV cache priming. Adaptive slice (grow slice size on measured latency) should trade-off and reduce p99.

Setup summary (notes to self):
- Model: open-llama-13B-ish quantized fp16 -> served with baseline kernels.
- Fleet: 2x A100-80GB equivalent (shared test cluster on dev pool), single node per run for easier telemetry mapping.
- Runtime flags: --continuous-batching on, --slot-slicing=[none|fixed:8|adaptive], --kv-cache-prefill=[true|false], --batch-window-ms=6
- Workload generator: synthetic client that sends 1–8 request bundles (tokens 50–250) with Poisson arrivals. Two scenarios:
  * Spike: background qps 40, spike to 420 for 12s at t=10s
  * Ramp: linear ramp 0 -> 300 qps over 30s
- Each experiment repeated 6 times, random seed rotated, collect per-request latencies + sampling of GPU metrics every 5s.

Key config variants run (note ids):
- B0: baseline (no slot slicing, kv-cache-prefill=false)
- B1: baseline + kv-cache-prefill=true
- S8: fixed slice size 8 (8 logical slots), kv-cache-prefill=false
- SA: adaptive slice, initial slice=4, grow factor=1.5, kv-cache-prefill=false
- SA+prefill: adaptive + kv-cache-prefill=true

Representative results (aggregated across runs; numbers are median of medians; see attached CSVs):

ASCII table (first 60s window):

| Run    | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | max (ms) | QPS peak | GPU util (%) | KV hit (%) |
|--------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------:|--------------:|-----------:|
| B0     | 18       | 120      | 480      | 1200     | 420       | 62           | 12         |
| B1     | 16       | 95       | 260      | 520      | 420       | 65           | 78         |
| S8     | 22       | 140      | 820      | 2500     | 420       | 58           | 22         |
| SA     | 19       | 110      | 310      | 730      | 420       | 61           | 20         |
| SA+prefill | 17   | 102      | 280      | 600      | 420       | 64           | 80         |

Observations / interpretation:
- KV cache prefill (B1, SA+prefill) is the single biggest win for p99 during cold-to-warm windows; consistent with hypothesis that priming KV items eliminates expensive mem copies and repeated kernel setups.
- Fixed small slices (S8) worsen p99 significantly — likely due to more frequent kernel context switches and multiple independent attempts to initialize attention buffers. Max latencies (2500ms) show repeated stalls from kernel warmup + GPU page faults (see GPU logs).
- Adaptive slice reduced worst-case p99 by ~2.6x vs S8 and approaches baseline+prefill when combined with prefill. The growth policy allowed fewer racing slice inits while retaining concurrency benefits.
- p95 improvements were smaller; slot slicing trades median latency for isolation at high qps but only if prefill is enabled.
- GPU util reported dips during the first 15s for S8 runs — looks like under-utilization due to per-slice throttling.

Run notes / debugging traces to pull:
- GH PR 812 includes the runtime hooks I used to toggle slice behavior; Instrumentation TODO: add per-slice kernel init timestamps (not present in current builds).
- Attachments: drive:charts/slot-slice-warmup-2025-11-04.png (time-series p99 + KV hit), drive:csvs/slot-slice-runs-2025-11-04.csv
- Jira INF-2143 contains the incident notes where customer pool saw p99 spikes after autoscale (useful context).

Quick micro-checks I ran (manual):
- Repeat S8 with batch-window-ms=12 -> p99 drops ~20% but p50 rises 6% (longer batch window reduces context switches).
- Swap kernel selection to 'fallback-fast' mode -> S8 p99 improved slightly, which implies kernel selection jitter contributes to variance.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we pre-warm kernels lazily (background kernel init) when autoscaler is provisioning nodes? Risks: extra memory + startup time. Idea: dedicate a tiny 'bootstrap' thread that runs a reduced synthetic forward to trigger kernel paths and KV touch.
- Add per-slice backoff jitter to reduce synchronized races for kernel init. How to pick distribution? (log-normal vs uniform).
- Correlate p99 spikes with memory page fault counters and driver-level 'cudaMalloc' slow paths — need deeper infra hooks.
- Evaluate effect across heterogeneous GPUs (RTX-ish vs A100) — does fixed slicing behave worse on smaller-memory GPUs?

Actionable next steps (owner in parens):
- Add per-slice kernel init tracing (Elara)
- Prototype background kernel pre-warm worker on new nodes (Ravi)
- Run longer 5-minute runs to see steady-state transition behavior (Marta + Elara)
- Schedule a short sync with Runtime + SRE to review INF-2143 overlap and share artifacts (invite list: runtime, sre, solutions-eng)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Compress CSVs and upload to drive, add a short deck for run leads.
- Check crash logs on node-a3 for S8/rep3 (driver OOM warnings present).
- If adaptive slice policy looks stable, consider a small canary on staging dedicated pools.

Closing thought: slot-slicing is promising for steady isolation but it's fragile during warmup unless we either prefill caches or coordinate kernel initialization. Prefill seems the highest-ROI change with lowest runtime complexity.
